language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Primitive values are immutable, while object values are mutable and assigned by reference.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: Assigning an object or array copies the reference, not the object. Mutating through any reference changes the shared object. const protects binding reassignment, not object contents.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: const a = {}; const b = a; b.x = 1; Object.freeze(obj)
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Shared references are central to state bugs, safe refactors, and API design.
common_misuse: Assuming assignment clones
Mutating input parameters without documenting
Using shallow clone for nested state
debugging_symptoms: Caller data changes after function call
Nested object still shared after spread
tests_or_checks: Check every mutation method and property write
Test aliasing by keeping original reference
Distinguish shallow and deep copy needs
safe_refactor_notes: Document ownership of objects
Use copies at boundaries when caller-owned data must be preserved
Do not replace mutation with copying if identity observers rely on it

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Objects can inherit properties from a prototype chain.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: Property reads search own properties first, then prototypes. Property writes usually create or set own properties unless accessors or special cases apply. Classes use prototypes for methods.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: Object.create(proto), obj.__proto__ legacy, Object.getPrototypeOf(obj), class C { method(){} }
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Prototype lookup explains method sharing, inheritance, shadowing, and many confusing ownership checks.
common_misuse: Using in when own-property check is required
Mutating built-in prototypes
Assuming class fields and prototype methods are equivalent
debugging_symptoms: Method exists but not as own property
Enumeration includes inherited key with for/in
safe_refactor_notes: Moving methods between instance and prototype changes identity and memory behavior
Preserve accessors and super behavior

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Different reflection APIs report different sets of properties.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: Own versus inherited, enumerable versus non-enumerable, string-keyed versus symbol-keyed properties determine what Object.keys, for/in, JSON.stringify, spread, Object.getOwnPropertyNames, Object.getOwnPropertySymbols, and Reflect.ownKeys see.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: Object.keys(obj), for (let k in obj), Object.hasOwn(obj,k), Reflect.ownKeys(obj)
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Copying, serialization, validation, and review tools can miss properties if they use the wrong reflection API.
common_misuse: Using for/in without ownership filter
Expecting JSON/spread to preserve non-enumerable or symbol keys
Ignoring getters during spread/copy
safe_refactor_notes: Choose reflection API intentionally before refactoring copies
Preserve descriptors when required

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Arrays are objects with special indexed properties and a length property; they may have holes.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: length is one greater than the largest array index and can be set directly. Sparse arrays have missing elements rather than present undefined values. Methods differ in how they handle holes.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: arr.length, arr[i], Array(n), delete arr[i], arr.push(x), arr.splice(i,1)
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: List-like code breaks when length is treated as proof every element exists.
common_misuse: Creating Array(n) and expecting values
delete for removal instead of splice
Assuming map/forEach callbacks visit holes
debugging_symptoms: Length larger than count of present elements
tests_or_checks: Test dense, sparse, and explicit undefined arrays
safe_refactor_notes: Do not refactor loops/methods across sparse arrays without hole tests
Normalize to dense arrays when list semantics are needed

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Array methods encode common traversal and transformation patterns.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: forEach, map, filter, reduce, find, some, every, sort and related methods call callbacks with element, index, and array. Mutating during iteration or relying on sparse behavior can surprise.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: arr.map(fn), arr.filter(fn), arr.reduce(fn, init), arr.sort(compare), for...of
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Array method choice directly affects returned value, mutation, order, and edge cases.
common_misuse: Using forEach expecting a returned array
Using sort without numeric comparator
Mutating the iterated array in callback
Omitting reduce initial value for possible empty array
tests_or_checks: Test empty, one-element, sparse, and mixed-type arrays
safe_refactor_notes: Switch between loops and methods only with tests for holes and mutation
Keep sort mutation visible

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Some objects look like arrays because they have length and numeric properties but are not arrays.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: Array-like objects may not inherit Array.prototype methods. They can often be converted with Array.from or spread if iterable, but length-only array-like and iterable are distinct concepts.
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Browser and legacy APIs often return list-like values where array methods or live/static behavior matter.
common_misuse: Calling array methods directly on non-arrays
Assuming spread works on every length object
Assuming DOM collection liveness without checking
tests_or_checks: Use Array.from with mapping when needed
safe_refactor_notes: Normalize once at boundary
Do not change live collection behavior without browser tests

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Functions can be stored, passed, returned, and invoked like other values.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: Function declarations, function expressions, and arrow functions create callable objects. Functions may have properties, close over scope, and differ in this/arguments/new behavior.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: function f(){}, const f = function(){}, const f = x => x, callback(fn)
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Callbacks, higher-order APIs, modules, and event handlers depend on functions as first-class values.
common_use: Store behavior in objects or maps
common_misuse: Invoking when a reference is needed
Passing this-dependent method without binding
Assuming arrow and function are interchangeable
debugging_symptoms: Function cannot be used as constructor
tests_or_checks: Check this, arguments, and new requirements
safe_refactor_notes: Preserve function form when this/arguments/constructor behavior matters
Name functions when stack traces matter

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: A function can remember variables from the lexical scope where it was created.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: Nested functions and returned callbacks retain access to outer lexical bindings. They observe the variable binding, not an automatic deep snapshot of every value.
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Closures power callbacks, modules, private state patterns, and many asynchronous bugs.
common_misuse: Expecting captured variable to reset automatically
Capturing mutable loop/state by accident
Leaking memory through long-lived closures over large objects
tests_or_checks: Test repeated calls and concurrent callbacks
safe_refactor_notes: Pass explicit parameters when snapshot is intended
Reset closure state in test setup
Avoid capturing broad objects unnecessarily

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: The value of this depends on how a function is invoked, not only where it is defined.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: Method calls set this to the receiver. Plain function calls, constructor calls, call/apply/bind, event callbacks, and arrow functions differ. Arrow functions capture lexical this and cannot be used as ordinary methods requiring dynamic this.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: obj.m(), f(), new C(), f.call(obj), f.bind(obj), () => this.x
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: this bugs are uniquely common in methods, callbacks, classes, event handlers, and extracted functions.
common_use: Use lexical this inside nested arrows
common_misuse: Passing obj.method directly as callback
Using arrow for prototype method needing receiver
Forgetting strict-mode plain-call this
debugging_symptoms: Method works in object call but not event/timer callback
tests_or_checks: Identify every this use and invocation form
safe_refactor_notes: Refactor methods to arrows only when receiver semantics are irrelevant
Bind at construction or call boundary, not randomly inside logic
